t: In front of you is a bronze statue of Robert Clive, standing in King Charles Street, off Whitehall. It's by the sculptor John Tweed, and it's Grade II listed. It was unveiled in 1912 outside Gwydyr House, also in Whitehall, and moved here in 1916. Clive, often called Clive of India, was the first British Governor of the Bengal Presidency. He's widely credited with laying the foundation of East India Company rule in Bengal, which is why he is commemorated in this part of government London, though his legacy is a contested one.
